extracted.intended_audience: mathematics educators, teacher trainers, and researchers in math education
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and discussion about introducing Problem-Based Learning (PBL) into university courses to prepare future mathematics teachers, describing PBL's features, teacher responsibilities, and obstacles to adoption in pre-service training.

rubrics_metrics.name: PBL as constructivist learner-centered approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Problem-based learning (PBL) is a constructivist learner-centered instructional approach based on the analysis, resolution and discussion of a given problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize learner-centered activities centered on a concrete problem; design tasks that require analysis, resolution, and group discussion rather than purely didactic lecturing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability/applicability to mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: PBL can be applied to any subject and is especially useful for the teaching of mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select problems that expose mathematical structure and reasoning; favor tasks illustrating how mathematics is used, demonstrating particular usefulness of PBL in math contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teacher role: increased responsibility and facilitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Compared to 'traditional' teaching, PBL requires increased responsibility for teachers: in addition to presenting mathematical knowledge, teachers must engage students in gathering information and using their knowledge to solve problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train teachers to act as facilitators—scaffold information gathering, prompt application of prior knowledge, guide discussions, and resist reverting to pure exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for future teachers to recognize PBL effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: It is crucial that future teachers become aware of PBL's effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include reflective components and evidence of learning gains in training so prospective teachers can observe and evaluate PBL outcomes themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion in pre-service training to overcome adoption obstacles
rubrics_metrics.description: A main obstacle to awareness and adoption is that future teachers often did not encounter PBL in their own pre-service training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate PBL experiences into teacher education curricula to ensure exposure; address curricular gaps that leave trainees unfamiliar with the methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiential learning: have future teachers 'experience mathematics'
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce PBL in university courses so future math teachers experience mathematics themselves via problem-solving activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design teacher-training courses that let trainees participate as learners in PBL activities, so they gain first-hand experience of the method's processes and benefits.
